My main point is simple: the

The algorithms are not constructed on proper and robust world models, but instead are built to autocomplete, based on sophisticated pattern-matching. As a result, AGI will remain a dream and the magical projections of exponential growth, which defy economic and financial logic and fatally ignore unforgiving physical (analogue) constraints imposed by the electricity grid, the construction industry, and the shortage of (skilled) workers who are needed to help build the additional data center infrastructure, will turn out to be wrong.

However, the generic LLMs are different from specific, domain-specific AI tools that are already being used in many scientific disciplines, such as protein science,Footnote2 code generation and pharmaceutical research, and to great effect. Targeted machine-learning systems can manage load on the electricity grid more effectively and help reduce carbon emissions in trucking, shipping, steelmaking and mining industries. Each use case should be scrutinized for its utility, the biases and risks it might introduce, and its propensity to destroy jobs that depend on human judgment. However, these domain-specific tools do not require the massive capital expenditures on GPUs and data-center infrastructure that are needed for the LLMs; hence, investments in customized AI tools, trained on datasets specific to a particular domain, such as legal documents, financial reports, or technical literature, may well pay-off, unlike the megalomanic expenditures on training, inference, and computeFootnote3 for the generic LLMs. This article focuses on the latter.

The fact that the AI industry is not only the principal source of growth in an otherwise sclerotic U.S. economy (Storm Citation2025), but is also driven by a concentrated set of hyper-scalers engaging in ‘circular’ transactions based on aggressively optimistic long-term cash flow-generating potential should be cause for worry (Arun Citation2025). We now laugh at the utter foolishness of some of the richest merchants in Amsterdam who at the height of Tulip Mania in February 1637 were buying exotic tulip bulbs at ridiculous prices of around 5,000 Dutch guilders per pound (Goldgar Citation2007)—approximately two million Euros today, equal to the cost of an upscale Amsterdam canal house.Footnote4 But rest assured: we will be the butt of the jokes of future historians—for not recognizing the current AI mania for what it is: a bubble.Footnote5

To be clear, cracks are showing and worries of an AI bubble are intensifying (e.g., Schmidt and Xu Citation2025; Thornhill Citation2025), and rapidly so. In October-November 2025, several hedge funds trimmed their stakes in some of the largest seven tech firms (the so-called ‘Magnificent Seven’) (Sen Citation2025), especially after warnings from the CEOs of Goldman SachsFootnote6 and Morgan Stanley (Saini and Nishant Citation2025). Following growing concerns about Oracle’s massive data-center debt, Oracle’s five-year CDS spread increased by 80 basis points in November 2025 and the trading volume for Oracle’s credit derivatives surged as well. The CDS spread on Coreweave’s debt surged as well (Kedrosky Citation2025c). In early December 2025, OpenAI declared Code Red (Jin Citation2025), after losing 6% of its users in a week due to Google’s new Gemini-3 model. By any reasonable measure OpenAI has squandered the sizable lead it once had. If investors decide to opt out, it will be impossible to keep the operation afloat and OpenAI’s predicted valuation could drop, perhaps dramatically. If OpenAI goes down, the inflated stock price of Nvidia will drop as well.
